title: A pi extension is a default-exported factory function that receives ExtensionAPI
detail: Every pi extension exports `export default function (pi: ExtensionAPI)` (sync or async). The factory body subscribes to events via pi.on(...) and registers tools/commands/shortcuts/flags via pi.registerTool / pi.registerCommand / pi.registerShortcut / pi.registerFlag. TypeScript is loaded via jiti — no build step needed. Available imports: @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent (ExtensionAPI types), typebox (Type.Object schema), @earendil-works/pi-ai (StringEnum), @earendil-works/pi-tui. Node built-ins (node:fs, node:path) are available. If the factory returns a Promise, pi awaits it before session_start / resources_discover, so async init completes first. Project-local extensions under .pi/extensions/*.ts load only after the project is trusted; global extensions live in ~/.pi/agent/extensions/*.ts.

title: registerTool execute has 5 positional args (toolCallId, params, signal, onUpdate, ctx) and returns {content, details, isError?}
detail:
> [!warning] The execute callback signature is async execute(toolCallId, params, signal, onUpdate, ctx) — all five positional, no options object.
The return shape is { content: [{type:'text', text}], details: <any>, isError?: boolean }. Set isError:true (not a throw) to signal a tool error to the LLM. onUpdate?.({content:[...]}) streams partial progress before the final return. ctx carries cwd and session context. The params object is already schema-validated against the typebox Type.Object parameters definition before execute runs, so you can trust param types. signal is an AbortSignal — check signal.aborted in long-running tools.

title: Tool parameters use typebox Type.Object with Type.Optional and StringEnum — not Zod or JSON Schema literals
detail: pi tool parameter schemas are authored with typebox: Type.Object({ name: Type.String({description:'...'}), count: Type.Optional(Type.Number({minimum:1})) }). For Google-compatible enums, import StringEnum from @earendil-works/pi-ai (NOT typebox's Type.Union of literals for enums exposed to the model — StringEnum renders the provider-native enum). Every field should carry a description: it becomes the schema doc the LLM sees. Optional fields use Type.Optional(...). The parameters object is what the LLM is told to fill; keep it focused and avoid giant enum blobs in the always-on schema (split heavy per-enum prose into a lazy-loaded _help tool instead).

title: Spawn subagents with a per-action RESTRICTED tool allowlist, not the full tool set
detail: When an extension spawns an isolated subagent (e.g. via runSubagentWithRetry from pi-obsidian), pass an explicit toolsCsv of ONLY the tools that action needs. Example from pi-knowledge-card: zk_card add uses ADD_TOOLS=[obsidian_search, obsidian_query, obsidian_read, obsidian_create, obsidian_append_section, obsidian_update_frontmatter, obsidian_list]; zk_card remove uses REMOVE_TOOLS=[obsidian_read, obsidian_search, obsidian_delete]; zk_ask uses RAG_TOOLS=[obsidian_search, obsidian_query, obsidian_read, obsidian_list]. A restricted allowlist (1) focuses the subagent on the task, (2) prevents tool contamination where the subagent calls unrelated tools, (3) shrinks the schema cost on the subagent's context. Export the allowlist constants so the CLI and extension import the SAME sets and never drift.

title: Delegate vault resolution to pi-obsidian resolveVault — never roll a simplified resolver
detail:
> [!warning] A simplified resolver that only checks an env var + cwd/'vault' fails at runtime when the vault is registered via config or the Obsidian app.
Always call pi-obsidian's resolveVault(cwd) (the multi-tier resolver: OB_VAULT_PATH env -> run-dir obsidian_config.json -> Obsidian app -> cwd/vault walk). The hub asks its forward-dep to SERVE vault resolution rather than reimplementing it — this reads the run-dir config the simplified resolver missed. pi-knowledge-card's knowledge_query and graph_health tools both delegate to resolveKnowledgeVault -> resolveVault. For deterministic test injection, expose a __setVaultResolverForTest(fn|null) seam that overrides the resolver in tests and restores it (null = use real).

title: Guard cross-package tool-name contracts by loading the REAL dependency extension in a test
detail: When an extension names another package's tools in a string allowlist (e.g. obsidian_distill, obsidian_search), a rename in the dependency breaks the allowlist silently at runtime. Catch it at TEST time: allowlists.test.mjs loads the REAL pi-obsidian extension via a fake-pi registerTool collector, then asserts every obsidian_* name in the allowlist is actually registered by the loaded extension. This is a cross-package contract guard — it fails the moment pi-obsidian renames a tool the allowlist references. Pattern: makeFakePi() captures registerTool calls into a Set; import the dep's default factory; call it with fakePi; assert allowlist.every(name => registered.has(name)).

title: Share pure task-builder functions + allowlists between the extension and the CLI so they never drift
detail: The tool's execute() body builds a task string and calls a runner. Extract that string-building into PURE exported functions (buildDistillTask, buildRagTask, buildAddTask, ...) with NO I/O, and export the tool allowlists (DISTILL_TOOLS, RAG_TOOLS, ...) as constants. Then BOTH the extension's execute() AND the CLI command import the same builders + allowlists. Benefit: a change to the task template or allowlist updates both surfaces in one edit; a rename breaks the CLI at BUILD time (loud) instead of diverging at runtime. The extension module is the SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH; the CLI commands are thin shells. Unit-test the pure builders directly (no subagent/LLM needed).

title: bun:test mock.module() is process-global — a stub in one test FILE leaks into others under plain bun test
detail:
> [!warning] Under plain `bun test` (no --isolate), all test files share ONE process, so mock.module() patches a module process-globally and the stub leaks across files.
If file A mocks pi-obsidian's runSubagentWithRetry and file B exercises the real pi-obsidian parser, A's stub clobbers B's real import. Two resolutions: (1) prefer splitting the mocked export into its own module so only the consumer under test imports the stub; (2) rely on the fact that bun test isolates each test FILE only when --isolate is passed. The clean fix is structural: don't mock a module that another test file exercises for real. toolWiring.test.mjs (.mjs extension, mocks the whole obsidian module) and the .ts contract tests (import the real obsidian parser) coexist because the mock is scoped to the wiring file's concerns.

title: Use OB_VAULT_PATH (resolveVault Tier-1a) to point all vault tools at a temp dir for deterministic E2E tests
detail: For a true end-to-end test of vault tools that needs real file I/O but must NOT touch the production vault, set process.env.OB_VAULT_PATH = mkdtempSync(...) in beforeEach (save/restore the original in afterEach). resolveVault checks OB_VAULT_PATH FIRST (Tier-1a, wins over run-dir config and the Obsidian-app fallback), so EVERY tool that resolves the vault — zk_ingest, knowledge_query, graph_health, and even the vaultHeader formatter — writes/reads the temp dir. This avoids mocking the whole pi-obsidian module (which would break the real parseFrontmatter/getIndex the deterministic library needs). bun:test isolates each test FILE in its own process, so the env override cannot leak into sibling test files. Call invalidateCache(vault) between write/read phases so the cached VaultIndex sees new files.

title: promptGuidelines bullets are appended flat with no tool prefix — each bullet MUST name its tool explicitly
detail:
> [!warning] promptGuidelines entries are appended to the Guidelines section with NO tool-name prefix, so 'Use this tool when...' is ambiguous — the LLM cannot tell which tool 'this' means.
Always write 'Use my_tool when...' (name the tool explicitly). Contrast: promptSnippet is a one-line entry in the 'Available tools' list (opt-in, short), while promptGuidelines appends behavioral bullets to the default Guidelines section WHEN the tool is active. Use promptSnippet for discoverability ('what does this tool do, in one line') and promptGuidelines for routing rules ('when should the model pick this tool'). Both are optional; omitting promptSnippet keeps the tool out of the always-on Available-tools list (lower context cost).

title: Shrink always-on schema cost by splitting heavy per-enum prose into a lazy-loaded _help tool
detail: A tool whose parameters enum carries large prose descriptions (per-subcommand option keys, defaults, path rules) bloats the always-on API schema cost on every request even when the tool is never called. Proven lever: split the heavy per-enum/per-field prose into a sibling _help tool (e.g. flux2_help, ltx_help, obsidian_search_help) that the agent calls ON DEMAND before first use of a subcommand. Measured -38% to -73% schema cost on flux2/ltx/obsidian_search. The main tool's description stays terse ('call X_help for option keys before first use'); the lazy help tool returns the full reference only when invoked. This keeps the always-on context lean while preserving full discoverability.
